If the game says \"You have been disconnected\" with BLZ51914400 or BLZ51914500 right after you log in, Blizzard is blocking the sign-in.
Blizzard blocks game logins from a network it hasn\'t seen your account use, such as mobile data or a new Wi-Fi, or a login that arrives over Wi-Fi and mobile data at once.
1. Turn off any phone setting that uses Wi-Fi and mobile data together, such as Optimize network for speed in Settings, System, Network.
2. Tap Open battle.net and sign in there, on the same connection.
3. Come back to the app and start the game again.
4. Still getting BLZ51914500? Your password didn\'t match. Re-enter it with Change login.

If your Battle.net login has more than one WoW account, such as WoW1 and WoW2, choose the one to play. The Battle.net app lists them in its account menu. A change applies the next time you start the game.

For other problems, turn on debug logging, make the problem happen again, then share a debug report on your GitHub issue. The game won\'t start by itself while logging is on, so opening the app doesn\'t replace the game\'s logs. The report holds your device details, settings and logs. Email addresses and your saved login are removed from it.

Lossless Scaling\'s frame generation (LSFG) can raise the frame rate by adding generated frames, at the cost of a little input delay. It needs Lossless.dll from your own copy of Lossless Scaling on Steam: on your PC it\'s in Steam/steamapps/common/Lossless Scaling. Copy it to this device and choose it here. The in-game menu (Back) then has an LSFG tab to set it up.
This Lossless.dll doesn\'t have the frame generation shaders, so the game starts without frame generation. Choose the one from a current Steam install of Lossless Scaling.
